name: 3x4 membrane keypad
description: Phone-style 12-key matrix membrane keypad (1 2 3 / 4 5 6 / 7 8 9 / * 0 #): 12 passive switches wired as 4 rows x 3 columns, read by scanning with 7 GPIO pins. No chip and no power pin; contacts rated 30 V DC / 30 mA max (generic membrane keypad datasheet), used at the microcontroller's 3.3 V logic level. Sold as: Adafruit Membrane 3x4 Matrix Keypad (#419) and its many clones, 7-pin 0.1" ribbon in order R1, R2, R3, R4, C1, C2, C3.
eli5: A flat telephone-style keypad: pressing a key connects one row wire to one column wire, and your board works out which key it was.

pins.name: C1
pins.description: Column 1 (keys 1 4 7 *); header pin 5; use the GPIO's internal pull-up

pins.name: C2
pins.description: Column 2 (keys 2 5 8 0); header pin 6; use the GPIO's internal pull-up

pins.name: C3
pins.description: Column 3 (keys 3 6 9 #); header pin 7; use the GPIO's internal pull-up

buildNotes: Pin 1 of the ribbon is the left end with the keys facing you: R1, R2, R3, R4, C1, C2, C3 (Adafruit #419 pinout). Some clones differ, so if keys come out wrong, check with a multimeter: the 1 key joins R1 and C1.
No power wire: columns use the GPIO internal pull-ups, rows are driven low one at a time.
Leave rows that are not being scanned as inputs (high-impedance) so pressing two keys in one column cannot short two outputs together.
Debounce: confirm a key is still down about 20 ms after it is first seen.
Plug the ribbon into a 7-pin male header; avoid bending the flat tail sharply where it leaves the keypad, as the printed traces crack.

driver.code:
# 3x4 matrix membrane keypad (Adafruit #419 and its clones), MicroPython driver.
# The keypad is just 12 switches: each key joins one row wire (R1-R4) to one column wire (C1-C3).
# Scan: columns are inputs with pull-ups; one row at a time is driven low and any column that
# reads low has its key pressed. Rows that are not being scanned are left as inputs (high-impedance)
# so that two keys held in the same column can never short a high output to a low one.
import time

KEYS_3X4 = ('123', '456', '789', '*0#')


class Keypad:
    def __init__(self, row_pins, col_pins, keys=KEYS_3X4, debounce_ms=20):
        from machine import Pin
        self._Pin = Pin
        self.rows = [Pin(p, Pin.IN) for p in row_pins]
        self.cols = [Pin(p, Pin.IN, Pin.PULL_UP) for p in col_pins]
        self.keys = keys
        self.debounce_ms = debounce_ms
        self._last = None

    def scan(self):
        """Return the label of the key held right now, or None."""
        Pin = self._Pin
        found = None
        for r, row in enumerate(self.rows):
            row.init(Pin.OUT, value=0)
            time.sleep_us(10)  # let the membrane trace and pull-ups settle
            for c, col in enumerate(self.cols):
                if col.value() == 0 and found is None:
                    found = self.keys[r][c]
            row.init(Pin.IN)
        return found

    def get_key(self):
        """Return a key's label once, when it is newly pressed (debounced); otherwise None."""
        k = self.scan()
        if k is not None and k != self._last:
            time.sleep_ms(self.debounce_ms)
            if self.scan() != k:
                return None  # contact bounce or released: ignore
            self._last = k
            return k
        self._last = k
        return None

example.code:
from machine import Pin
import time
from keypad import Keypad

kp = Keypad(({R1}, {R2}, {R3}, {R4}), ({C1}, {C2}, {C3}))
while True:
    key = kp.get_key()
    if key:
        print('KEY=' + key)
    time.sleep_ms(10)
